baseline.title: End-to-end rota website guide
baseline.rootText:
No-brainer operating guide
        How to run the Duty Rota website from start to finish
        Use this section when a new rota board member needs to understand the whole workflow, the terms on screen, and what to fix when something looks wrong.
      
      
        Start With Members
        Open Template
      
    

    
      Guide Map
      
        Phase 1: Data Readiness
        Phase 2: Rota Generation
        Duty Eligibility
        Monthly Workflow
        Website Sections
        Admin Tools
        Important Terms
        Scores And Blocks
        Problems And Fixes
        Final Checklist
      
    

    
      
        Phase 1
        Data Readiness And Setup
        Do this before rota generation. If this phase is weak, every later page will show wrong candidates, wrong warnings, or blocked publish.
      
      
        
          1. Members
          Confirm active people, call level, designation, duplicates, and aliases.
          Open Members
        
        
          2. Leave
          Enter or import leave for the target month and resolve unknown names.
          Open Leave
        
        
          3. Units
          Enter or import unit postings and fix unknown units or unmapped people.
          Open Units
        
        
          4. Rota Setup
          Select the month scope, included units, and setup rules before template generation.
          Open Setup
        
      
      Start with Department Members because every import depends on clean names.Load Leave only after member names and aliases are clean enough to match.Load Unit Management only after members are clean and the target month is selected.Use Rota Setup last, after people, leave, and unit postings are ready.Move to Rota Template only when Phase 1 has no unknown names, wrong months, or obvious setup gaps.
    

    
      
        Phase 2
        Rota Generation And Assignment
        Use this phase after Phase 1 is clean. The goal is to create the month template, assign people under each duty in call-wise order, and avoid unsafe shortcuts.
      
      
        
          1. Generate Template
          Open Rota Template, select the correct month, and generate the empty duty structure.
          Open Template
        
        
          2. Assign Duty-Wise
          Open each day and fill Main, CB, RC, PAC, and other duties separately.
          Assign Duties
        
        
          3. Check Candidates
          Use suggested candidates, leave warnings, unit fit, call level, and workload signals before saving.
          Open Review
        
        
          4. Use Auto-Fill Carefully
          Run Safe Auto-Fill only when source data is clean, then manually review every filled slot.
          Review Filled Slots
        
      
      Open Rota Template and confirm the month shown on screen is the month you want.Generate the empty template only after Phase 1 is complete.Switch to Statistics to confirm unit-wise, date-wise, weekend, duty-type, and call-level slot distribution.Read cluster labels beside units: Unit 1 (3A), Unit 1 (3B), or Unit 1 (3C) means that slot is restricted to that 3rd-call subgroup.Open one day at a time and review duties in fixed duty order.Under each duty, assign slots call-wise so the day is easy to read and audit.Prefer candidates without leave, unit mismatch, recent-duty, or workload warnings.If you override a warning, enter a reason that another board member can understand later.Use Safe Auto-Fill as a draft helper, not as final approval.After assignment, open Rota Review before publishing.
    

    
      Duty Eligibility: Category, Call Level, And Eligibility Groups
      Rota Rules has two different ideas that sound similar. Duty category describes the type of duty. Eligibility controls which people can actually do it.
      
        Duty categoryUsed for duty counting and grouping, such as Main duty, RC duty, Shift duty, PAC, or Schell duty. It is not a member list.
        Call levels allowedThe normal eligibility rule. Main 3rd Call should allow 3rd Call only. Main 1st Call should allow 1st Call only.
        Specific groups allowedUse this only when a smaller selected pool inside the allowed call level can do the duty, such as Schell eligible or PAC seniors.
        Groups excludedUse this when most of a call level can do a duty, but a named subgroup should not be used.
      
      For ordinary duties, set Call levels allowed and leave Specific groups allowed blank.For Main 3rd Call, choose 3rd Call in Call levels allowed. Do not create a separate Main duty member group.For Schell, PAC, Main Shift, RC Shift, or PB Shift, first create the eligibility group in Admin Tools > Eligibility Groups.Return to Rota Rules and select that group under Specific groups allowed for the relevant duty.Remember: Duty category affects rota counting and grouping; it does not decide the member list by itself.
    

    
      Monthly Workflow
      Sign in and open Overview to confirm the API is online.Open Department Members and confirm active people, historical people, position, and call level.Open Leave and enter or import all leave for the target month.Open Unit Management and enter or import each person's unit posting for the month.Open Rota Setup, select included units, confirm rules, and lock the month scope.Open Rota Template and generate the empty duty template.Open each day and assign people duty-wise in call order.Use Safe Auto-Fill only after people, leave, units, and setup are clean.Open Rota Review and clear open slots, hard blocks, warnings, workload issues, and exchanges.Open Publish & Export, complete final approval, publish the rota, and download Excel.
    

    
      
        Overview
        The starting dashboard. Use it to confirm workload trends, API health, and quick entry points before doing detailed rota work.
        If Overview cannot load, the backend or analysis API may be offline.Use it as a quick health check, not as the final rota approval page.
      
      
        Duty Analysis
        Shows historical duty burden, weekend load, duty categories, postings, promotions, and manual review items.
        Fix invalid names or unmapped duties before trusting historical fairness.Open a person profile when a number looks unusual.
      
      
        Department Members
        The master people list. A person must be correct here before they can be safely used in leave, unit posting, and rota assignment.
        Check active status, call level, designation, aliases, and duplicates.Historical members should not be used for new monthly duties unless intentionally reactivated.
      
      
        Leave
        Records who is unavailable and why. Leave affects candidate selection, warnings, hard blocks, and publish readiness.
        Import leave into the correct month.Resolve unknown names before generating or reviewing the rota.Check leave pressure when many people are unavailable on the same date.
      
      
        Unit Management
        Stores monthly unit postings. Unit availability controls which people are suitable for unit-specific duties.
        Import unit postings after member names are clean.Resolve unknown units and unknown people.Check unit staffing warnings before template generation.
      
      
        Rota Setup
        Defines the month scope, included units, and configuration used to create the duty template.
        Confirm month, included units, and rules before generating.Do not keep changing setup after assignments unless you understand the impact.
      
      
        Rota Template
        The main work area for daily duties. Open a day, review slots under each duty, check allocation statistics, and assign people in call-wise order.
        Look at Main, CB, RC, PAC, and other duty groups separately.Unit labels with (3A), (3B), or (3C) are restricted to that matching 3rd-call eligibility subgroup.Use Statistics to confirm the split by unit, day, Saturday, Sunday, duty type, call level, and forced review slots.Forced review means every unit was hard blocked, so the engine filled the least damaging unit instead of leaving the duty empty.Use candidates as guidance; lower priority score means the system prefers that person first.Override only with a clear reason.Fast mode is useful when a heavy month loads slowly.
      
      
        Rota Review
        The validation dashboard for open slots, warnings, hard blocks, workload balance, and exchange approvals.
        A hard block means fix the rota or enter a justified override.Open slots must be assigned before publish.If review loads too long, use the template and check backend status.
      
      
        Publish & Export
        The final approval page. It checks whether the rota is ready, records approval, and exports the Excel output.
        Do not publish with unresolved blockers.Warnings should be fixed or intentionally accepted.Download Excel only after the final published state is correct.
      
    

    
      Admin Tools
      
        Rota RulesControls each duty's allowed call levels, restricted eligibility groups, and duty category.
        Eligibility GroupsCreates selected member pools inside a parent call level for special duties such as Schell, PAC, Main Shift, RC Shift, or PB Shift.
        MappingsConnects messy imported duty names or member labels to clean system terms.
        Historical ImportLoads older rota data for analysis and fairness context.
        Login AccountsCreates and manages rota board, computer admin, and superadmin access.
        DiagnosticsShows backend counts, health signals, and raw diagnostic payloads for troubleshooting.
      
    

    
      Important Terms
      
        Duty slotOne duty requirement on one date that needs one assigned person.
        Duty categoryThe category of duty used for counting and grouping. It is not a group of people.
        Call levelThe duty seniority or call category used for matching people to slots.
        Eligibility groupA selected member pool inside one parent call level for special restricted duties.
        Unit postingWhere a person is posted for the selected month.
        CandidateA person suggested by the system as suitable for a slot, based on unit posting, call level, eligibility group, leave, rest, and workload.
        Priority scoreThe ranking number beside a suggested member. Lower is better. The system adds penalty points for same weekday/weekend duty load, total month duties, 24-hour duties, rest concerns, staffing pressure, and override needs.
        SafeA suggested member with no known person-specific leave, rest, call-level, subgroup, or validation blocker for that slot.
        Needs ReviewA suggested member may be usable, but the board must review a warning such as pending leave, staffing pressure, or another soft concern.
        BlockedA suggested member has a hard conflict such as approved leave, same-day duty, post-24hr rest block, or a validation error. Do not use unless the system allows an override and the board records a reason.
        Hard blockedA slot or review item has a serious rule conflict. It normally stops final publish until fixed. Examples include no eligible members, too few available members, hard safety thresholds, wrong call level, or wrong eligibility subgroup.
        Forced review slotA generated template slot where all units were hard blocked, but the engine still filled the fairest least-damaging unit so the rota sheet has no empty duty cell.
        WarningA softer problem that needs review but may be accepted with judgment.
        OverrideA deliberate decision to keep an assignment despite a rule concern. The reason should be clear enough for another board member to understand later.
        Safe Auto-FillAutomatic draft assignment that avoids known unsafe choices where possible.
      
    

    
      Suggested Members, Score, And Hard Blocks
      In the rota day popup, suggested members are only a decision aid. The board still has to decide and save the assignment.
      The system first finds people posted to the same unit on the slot date.It then applies the duty rule: allowed call level, eligibility group, and excluded group.It separates people into Safe, Needs Review, and Blocked.It calculates a priority score. Lower score means better suggested order.The strongest current fairness rule is same weekday/weekend load. For a Friday slot, people with fewer weekday duties rank higher. For a Saturday or Sunday slot, people with fewer weekend duties rank higher.After that, the score also considers total monthly duties, 24-hour duties, weekend 24-hour duties, same duty category, same campus, rest gap, staffing pressure, and override needs.Use Safe candidates first. Review candidates need board judgment and usually an override reason. Blocked candidates should normally be avoided.Hard blocked slots must be fixed before publish unless the workflow explicitly allows a justified override.
    

    
      
        Common Problems
        Page keeps loading: refresh once, check API status, then try a lighter view or fast mode.Person is missing: open Department Members and confirm active status and spelling.Wrong call level: update the member call level before assigning duties.No candidates: check leave, unit posting, call level, and rota setup scope.Publish disabled: open Rota Review and clear blockers first.
      
      
        Do Not Do
        Do not publish with unresolved hard blocks or unreviewed forced slots.Do not import files into the wrong month.Do not clear generated draft duties casually.Do not change rota rules mid-month without board agreement.Do not assume Safe Auto-Fill completed every slot correctly.
      
    

    
      Final Monthly Checklist
      Members checked.Leave imported and unresolved rows fixed.Unit postings imported and unresolved rows fixed.Rota setup confirmed.Template generated.Duty slots assigned call-wise under each duty.Rota Review warnings and blockers handled.Exchange requests approved or rejected.Publish checklist passed.Final Excel exported.

candidate.title: End-to-end rota website guide
candidate.rootText:
No-brainer operating guide
        How to run the Duty Rota website from start to finish
        Use this section when a new rota board member needs to understand the whole workflow, the terms on screen, and what to fix when something looks wrong.
      
      
        Start With Members
        Open Template
      
    

    
      Guide Map
      
        Phase 1: Data Readiness
        Phase 2: Rota Generation
        Duty Eligibility
        Monthly Workflow
        Website Sections
        Admin Tools
        Important Terms
        Scores And Blocks
        Problems And Fixes
        Final Checklist
      
    

    
      
        Phase 1
        Data Readiness And Setup
        Do this before rota generation. If this phase is weak, every later page will show wrong candidates, wrong warnings, or blocked publish.
      
      
        
          1. Members
          Confirm active people, call level, designation, duplicates, and aliases.
          Open Members
        
        
          2. Leave
          Enter or import leave for the target month and resolve unknown names.
          Open Leave
        
        
          3. Units
          Enter or import unit postings and fix unknown units or unmapped people.
          Open Units
        
        
          4. Rota Setup
          Select the month scope, included units, and setup rules before template generation.
          Open Setup
        
      
      Start with Department Members because every import depends on clean names.Load Leave only after member names and aliases are clean enough to match.Load Unit Management only after members are clean and the target month is selected.Use Rota Setup last, after people, leave, and unit postings are ready.Move to Rota Template only when Phase 1 has no unknown names, wrong months, or obvious setup gaps.
    

    
      
        Phase 2
        Rota Generation And Assignment
        Use this phase after Phase 1 is clean. The goal is to create the month template, assign people under each duty in call-wise order, and avoid unsafe shortcuts.
      
      
        
          1. Generate Template
          Open Rota Template, select the correct month, and generate the empty duty structure.
          Open Template
        
        
          2. Assign Duty-Wise
          Open each day and fill Main, CB, RC, PAC, and other duties separately.
          Assign Duties
        
        
          3. Check Candidates
          Use suggested candidates, leave warnings, unit fit, call level, and workload signals before saving.
          Open Review
        
        
          4. Use Auto-Fill Carefully
          Run Safe Auto-Fill only when source data is clean, then manually review every filled slot.
          Review Filled Slots
        
      
      Open Rota Template and confirm the month shown on screen is the month you want.Generate the empty template only after Phase 1 is complete.Switch to Statistics to confirm unit-wise, date-wise, weekend, duty-type, and call-level slot distribution.Read cluster labels beside units: Unit 1 (3A), Unit 1 (3B), or Unit 1 (3C) means that slot is restricted to that 3rd-call subgroup.Open one day at a time and review duties in fixed duty order.Under each duty, assign slots call-wise so the day is easy to read and audit.Prefer candidates without leave, unit mismatch, recent-duty, or workload warnings.If you override a warning, enter a reason that another board member can understand later.Use Safe Auto-Fill as a draft helper, not as final approval.After assignment, open Rota Review before publishing.
    

    
      Duty Eligibility: Category, Call Level, And Eligibility Groups
      Rota Rules has two different ideas that sound similar. Duty category describes the type of duty. Eligibility controls which people can actually do it.
      
        Duty categoryUsed for duty counting and grouping, such as Main duty, RC duty, Shift duty, PAC, or Schell duty. It is not a member list.
        Call levels allowedThe normal eligibility rule. Main 3rd Call should allow 3rd Call only. Main 1st Call should allow 1st Call only.
        Specific groups allowedUse this only when a smaller selected pool inside the allowed call level can do the duty, such as Schell eligible or PAC seniors.
        Groups excludedUse this when most of a call level can do a duty, but a named subgroup should not be used.
      
      For ordinary duties, set Call levels allowed and leave Specific groups allowed blank.For Main 3rd Call, choose 3rd Call in Call levels allowed. Do not create a separate Main duty member group.For Schell, PAC, Main Shift, RC Shift, or PB Shift, first create the eligibility group in Admin Tools > Eligibility Groups.Return to Rota Rules and select that group under Specific groups allowed for the relevant duty.Remember: Duty category affects rota counting and grouping; it does not decide the member list by itself.
    

    
      Monthly Workflow
      Sign in and open Overview to confirm the API is online.Open Department Members and confirm active people, historical people, position, and call level.Open Leave and enter or import all leave for the target month.Open Unit Management and enter or import each person's unit posting for the month.Open Rota Setup, select included units, confirm rules, and lock the month scope.Open Rota Template and generate the empty duty template.Open each day and assign people duty-wise in call order.Use Safe Auto-Fill only after people, leave, units, and setup are clean.Open Rota Review and clear open slots, hard blocks, warnings, workload issues, and exchanges.Open Publish & Export, complete final approval, publish the rota, and download Excel.
    

    
      
        Overview
        The starting dashboard. Use it to confirm workload trends, API health, and quick entry points before doing detailed rota work.
        If Overview cannot load, the backend or analysis API may be offline.Use it as a quick health check, not as the final rota approval page.
      
      
        Duty Analysis
        Shows historical duty burden, weekend load, duty categories, postings, promotions, and manual review items.
        Fix invalid names or unmapped duties before trusting historical fairness.Open a person profile when a number looks unusual.
      
      
        Department Members
        The master people list. A person must be correct here before they can be safely used in leave, unit posting, and rota assignment.
        Check active status, call level, designation, aliases, and duplicates.Historical members should not be used for new monthly duties unless intentionally reactivated.
      
      
        Leave
        Records who is unavailable and why. Leave affects candidate selection, warnings, hard blocks, and publish readiness.
        Import leave into the correct month.Resolve unknown names before generating or reviewing the rota.Check leave pressure when many people are unavailable on the same date.
      
      
        Unit Management
        Stores monthly unit postings. Unit availability controls which people are suitable for unit-specific duties.
        Import unit postings after member names are clean.Resolve unknown units and unknown people.Check unit staffing warnings before template generation.
      
      
        Rota Setup
        Defines the month scope, included units, and configuration used to create the duty template.
        Confirm month, included units, and rules before generating.Do not keep changing setup after assignments unless you understand the impact.
      
      
        Rota Template
        The main work area for daily duties. Open a day, review slots under each duty, check allocation statistics, and assign people in call-wise order.
        Look at Main, CB, RC, PAC, and other duty groups separately.Unit labels with (3A), (3B), or (3C) are restricted to that matching 3rd-call eligibility subgroup.Use Statistics to confirm the split by unit, day, Saturday, Sunday, duty type, call level, and forced review slots.Forced review means every unit was hard blocked, so the engine filled the least damaging unit instead of leaving the duty empty.Use candidates as guidance; lower priority score means the system prefers that person first.Override only with a clear reason.Fast mode is useful when a heavy month loads slowly.
      
      
        Rota Review
        The validation dashboard for open slots, warnings, hard blocks, workload balance, and exchange approvals.
        A hard block means fix the rota or enter a justified override.Open slots must be assigned before publish.If review loads too long, use the template and check backend status.
      
      
        Publish & Export
        The final approval page. It checks whether the rota is ready, records approval, and exports the Excel output.
        Do not publish with unresolved blockers.Warnings should be fixed or intentionally accepted.Download Excel only after the final published state is correct.
      
    

    
      Admin Tools
      
        Rota RulesControls each duty's allowed call levels, restricted eligibility groups, and duty category.
        Eligibility GroupsCreates selected member pools inside a parent call level for special duties such as Schell, PAC, Main Shift, RC Shift, or PB Shift.
        MappingsConnects messy imported duty names or member labels to clean system terms.
        Historical ImportLoads older rota data for analysis and fairness context.
        Login AccountsCreates and manages rota board, computer admin, and superadmin access.
        DiagnosticsShows backend counts, health signals, and raw diagnostic payloads for troubleshooting.
      
    

    
      Important Terms
      
        Duty slotOne duty requirement on one date that needs one assigned person.
        Duty categoryThe category of duty used for counting and grouping. It is not a group of people.
        Call levelThe duty seniority or call category used for matching people to slots.
        Eligibility groupA selected member pool inside one parent call level for special restricted duties.
        Unit postingWhere a person is posted for the selected month.
        CandidateA person suggested by the system as suitable for a slot, based on unit posting, call level, eligibility group, leave, rest, and workload.
        Priority scoreThe ranking number beside a suggested member. Lower is better. The system adds penalty points for same weekday/weekend duty load, total month duties, 24-hour duties, rest concerns, staffing pressure, and override needs.
        SafeA suggested member with no known person-specific leave, rest, call-level, subgroup, or validation blocker for that slot.
        Needs ReviewA suggested member may be usable, but the board must review a warning such as pending leave, staffing pressure, or another soft concern.
        BlockedA suggested member has a hard conflict such as approved leave, same-day duty, post-24hr rest block, or a validation error. Do not use unless the system allows an override and the board records a reason.
        Hard blockedA slot or review item has a serious rule conflict. It normally stops final publish until fixed. Examples include no eligible members, too few available members, hard safety thresholds, wrong call level, or wrong eligibility subgroup.
        Forced review slotA generated template slot where all units were hard blocked, but the engine still filled the fairest least-damaging unit so the rota sheet has no empty duty cell.
        WarningA softer problem that needs review but may be accepted with judgment.
        OverrideA deliberate decision to keep an assignment despite a rule concern. The reason should be clear enough for another board member to understand later.
        Safe Auto-FillAutomatic draft assignment that avoids known unsafe choices where possible.
      
    

    
      Suggested Members, Score, And Hard Blocks
      In the rota day popup, suggested members are only a decision aid. The board still has to decide and save the assignment.
      The system first finds people posted to the same unit on the slot date.It then applies the duty rule: allowed call level, eligibility group, and excluded group.It separates people into Safe, Needs Review, and Blocked.It calculates a priority score. Lower score means better suggested order.The strongest current fairness rule is same weekday/weekend load. For a Friday slot, people with fewer weekday duties rank higher. For a Saturday or Sunday slot, people with fewer weekend duties rank higher.After that, the score also considers total monthly duties, 24-hour duties, weekend 24-hour duties, same duty category, same campus, rest gap, staffing pressure, and override needs.Use Safe candidates first. Review candidates need board judgment and usually an override reason. Blocked candidates should normally be avoided.Hard blocked slots must be fixed before publish unless the workflow explicitly allows a justified override.
    

    
      
        Common Problems
        Page keeps loading: refresh once, check API status, then try a lighter view or fast mode.Person is missing: open Department Members and confirm active status and spelling.Wrong call level: update the member call level before assigning duties.No candidates: check leave, unit posting, call level, and rota setup scope.Publish disabled: open Rota Review and clear blockers first.
      
      
        Do Not Do
        Do not publish with unresolved hard blocks or unreviewed forced slots.Do not import files into the wrong month.Do not clear generated draft duties casually.Do not change rota rules mid-month without board agreement.Do not assume Safe Auto-Fill completed every slot correctly.
      
    

    
      Final Monthly Checklist
      Members checked.Leave imported and unresolved rows fixed.Unit postings imported and unresolved rows fixed.Rota setup confirmed.Template generated.Duty slots assigned call-wise under each duty.Rota Review warnings and blockers handled.Exchange requests approved or rejected.Publish checklist passed.Final Excel exported.

baseline.title: Hard limits, rest, unit cover and equal duties
baseline.rootText:
Superadmin only
        Limits for every rota
        Limits are the boundaries every rota stays inside: how many duties one person can be given, how long they rest after a 24-hour duty, how many people each unit keeps free, and how evenly duties are shared within a call level. Generation, auto-fill and the extra-duty layer all follow them.
      
      History
    
    
      Hard limitHard rule: never broken. Generation, auto-fill and the extra-duty layer never go past it; only a superadmin allocation can, and that is recorded.
      Can be exceededCan be exceeded, with a reason, and is reported. Review and Publish warn you when it does.
      GuideGuide only: warns or steers, never stops a duty.
    
    
      Using the default limits; nothing has been saved on this page yet.
      View only. Only a superadmin can change limits.
    
    Per member each monthRest after a 24-hour dutyUnit staffingEqual duties within a call levelExtra duties (justice)
  
    
    
    
      Per member each monthHow many duties of each kind one member should get in a calendar month. Every unit and campus is counted together. Leave a box blank for no limit.
      
    
    
    
      
        Max 24-hour duties per member per month
        Can be exceeded
      
      The most 24-hour duties one member should get in a calendar month, counting all units and campuses together. Automatic filling will not give a member a duty that takes them past this number. A rota board member can still go past it on purpose by writing a reason, and the extra-duty step may go past it when the only other choice is leaving a duty empty. Anyone over the limit is listed on the Publish screen and in the audit report.
      Example Set to 6: a member who already has 6 twenty-four-hour duties in June is not offered a 7th by automatic filling. If the board gives them a 7th anyway, it needs a reason and the member shows as over the limit.
    
    
      
      
      duties
    
      Blank = no limit
    Saved: No limit
    
    
    
  
    
      
        Max weekend 24-hour duties per member per month
        Can be exceeded
      
      The most 24-hour duties on a Saturday or Sunday that one member should get in a month, all units together. These also count towards the 24-hour limit above. Automatic filling will not give a member a duty that takes them past this number. A rota board member can still go past it on purpose by writing a reason, and the extra-duty step may go past it when the only other choice is leaving a duty empty. Anyone over the limit is listed on the Publish screen and in the audit report.
      Example Set to 2: a member who has 24-hour duties on two Saturdays in June is not given a Sunday 24-hour duty that month by automatic filling.
    
    
      
      
      duties
    
      Blank = no limit
    Saved: No limit
    
    
    
  
    
      
        Max duties of one duty family per member per month
        Can be exceeded
      
      Every duty belongs to a family set in Rota Rules (for example Main, CB, RC or PAC). This is the most duties of one family a member should get in a month, so nobody does only one kind of work. Duties of every length count, not only 24-hour duties. Automatic filling will not give a member a duty that takes them past this number. A rota board member can still go past it on purpose by writing a reason, and the extra-duty step may go past it when the only other choice is leaving a duty empty. Anyone over the limit is listed on the Publish screen and in the audit report.
      Example Set to 4: a member who already has 4 Main duties in June (say two Main 3rd Call and two Main Co-3rd Call) can still get a CB or RC duty, but not a 5th Main duty.
    
    
      
      
      duties
    
      Blank = no limit
    Saved: No limit
    
    
    
  
    
      
        Max duties at one campus per member per month
        Can be exceeded
      
      The most duties one member should do at the same campus in a month. The campus is the campus of the unit the duty belongs to. Use it to share work between campuses. Automatic filling will not give a member a duty that takes them past this number. A rota board member can still go past it on purpose by writing a reason, and the extra-duty step may go past it when the only other choice is leaving a duty empty. Anyone over the limit is listed on the Publish screen and in the audit report.
      Example Set to 5: a member with 5 duties at one campus in June can still be placed at another campus, but not a 6th time at the same campus.
    
    
      
      
      duties
    
      Blank = no limit
    Saved: No limit
    
    
    
  
    
  
    
      Rest after a 24-hour dutyProtected time off after a 24-hour duty. The rest rule is never broken by any part of the rota.
      
    
    
    
      
        Rest after a 24-hour duty
        Hard limit
      
      The fewest hours a member must have off after a 24-hour duty ends before any other duty starts. This is a hard rule: automatic filling, the extra-duty step, manual assignment and superadmin allocation all refuse a duty that would cut the rest short. It also works the other way: a 24-hour duty cannot be given if it would end too close to a duty the member already has.
      Example Set to 24: after a 24-hour duty from Monday 8 am to Tuesday 8 am, the member's next duty can start on Wednesday at 8 am at the earliest.
    
    
      
      
      hours
    
      
    Saved: 24 hours
    
    
    
  
    
      
        No elective work the day after a 24-hour duty (policy record)
        Guide
      
      Records the department policy that a member gets no elective (daytime) work on the day after a 24-hour duty. The rota does not read this switch today: the day-after block is set for each duty in Rota Rules ("Blocks elective next day"), and every 24-hour duty already has it. Changing this switch does not change any rota.
      Example On: matches the Rota Rules setting, so a member who finishes a 24-hour duty on Tuesday morning is not given elective work on Tuesday.
    
    
      
        
        On
      
    Saved: On
    
    
    
  
    
  
    
      Unit staffingHow many members a unit must keep free for its normal work before its duties are flagged or held.
      
    
    
    
      
        Members a unit must keep free (default)
        Can be exceeded
      
      How many eligible members of a unit must still be free (not on leave, not resting after a 24-hour duty, not already on duty) after a duty is given out, so the unit can still do its normal work. Each unit usually has its own number in Unit management, also per call level; this default is used only where a unit or duty has no number of its own, and only while "Always keep the minimum free" is on. A duty that would leave fewer free is held: template generation avoids it and marks it for review, auto-fill leaves it open, a board member can still fill it with a reason, and the extra-duty step may fill it with a member from another unit.
      Example Set to 1: in a unit of 6 eligible members where 5 are on leave or resting, giving the last one a duty would leave nobody free, so the duty is held for the board to decide.
    
    
      
      
      members
    
      
    Saved: 1 member
    
    
    
  
    
      
        Warn when this share of a unit is unavailable
        Guide
      
      When this share (or more) of a unit's eligible members is unavailable on a day, because of leave, rest after a 24-hour duty or another duty, that day's duties in the unit are flagged "needs review". It is a warning, not a stop: template generation still fills the duty and marks it, auto-fill leaves it for a person to decide, and a board member who places someone gives a reason. It must be lower than the hard-block share below.
      Example Set to 30%: in a unit of 10 eligible members, a day with 3 of them unavailable gets a "needs review" flag.
    
    
      
      
      %
    
      
    Saved: 30%
    
    
    
  
    
      
        Hold duties when this share of a unit is unavailable
        Can be exceeded
      
      When this share (or more) of a unit's eligible members would be unavailable on a day, that day's duties in the unit are held (hard blocked) to protect the unit's normal work. Template generation avoids them and, if it has no other choice, marks them for review; auto-fill leaves them open; a board member can still fill one with a reason; and the extra-duty step may fill it with a member from another unit. It must be higher than the warning share above.
      Example With 30% warning and 40% hold, in a unit of 10 eligible members: 3 unavailable gives a warning, 4 unavailable holds the duty.
    
    
      
      
      %
    
      
    Saved: 40%
    
    
    
  
    
      
        Always keep the minimum free
        Can be exceeded
      
      When on, a unit never drops below its minimum number of free members (the unit's own number in Unit management, or the default above), even when the percentages would allow it. This matters most in small units, where one person is a large share. When off, only the two percentages are checked.
      Example On: a unit whose minimum is 2 keeps 2 members free whatever the percentages say. Off: the same unit can drop to 1 free as long as the share unavailable stays below the hold share.
    
    
      
        
        On
      
    Saved: On
    
    
    
  
    
  
    
      Equal duties within a call levelMembers of the same call level should end the month with almost the same number of duties, whatever campus they work at.
      
    
    
    
      
        Allowed difference in duties within a call level
        Guide
      
      Within each call level, every member's total duties for the month (all campuses together) should be almost the same. This is the largest difference allowed between the member with the most duties and the member with the fewest. The rota aims for it; when leave or rest make it impossible, the Publish screen shows a warning for that call level, but publishing is not stopped. Duties added by the extra-duty step or by a superadmin are shown separately when they cause the difference.
      Example Set to 1: 3rd call has 130 duties and 40 members, so the target is 3.25 (3 or 4 each). Totals of 3 and 4 are fine; a member with 2 while another has 4 (a difference of 2) is flagged.
    
    
      
      
      duties
    
      
    Saved: 1 duty
    
    
    
  
    
      
        How the target is worked out
        Guide
      
      Each call level's target is its duties in the month divided by its members available that month. "Automatic" is the only choice for now; the targets table shows the numbers for the chosen month.
      Example Automatic: 4th call with 62 duties and 20 members has a target of 3.1 duties each.
    
    
      
        Automatic (duties divided by members)
      
    Saved: Automatic (duties divided by members)
    
    
    
  
    
      
        Targets for November 2026
          Target = the call level's duty slots in the month ÷ its members available that month. With a gap of 1, the busiest and the least busy member of a level may differ by at most 1 duty.
        Month
      
      No targets for November 2026 yet. They appear once the month's duty slots exist (generate the template in Rota Template).
      The extra-duty layer and superadmin allocations may break equality; Publish and the 360° report show when they do.
    
  
    
      Extra duties (justice)When the extra-duty step must ask someone to do more, it first asks whoever has done the fewest extra duties recently.
      
    
    
    
      
        Months of extra-duty history to count
        Guide
      
      When the extra-duty step must give someone an extra duty, it first asks the members who have done the fewest extra duties recently. This sets how far back "recently" goes. A longer period remembers older extra duties; a shorter one lets them drop off sooner. It changes who is asked first, never whether a duty can be filled.
      Example Set to 12: when choosing for June 2026, an extra duty done in July 2025 still counts, but one done in May 2025 no longer does.
    
    
      
      
      months
    
      
    Saved: 12 months
    
    
    
  
    
  
    
      
      
      View onlyOnly a superadmin can change limits.

candidate.title: Hard limits, rest, unit cover and equal duties
candidate.rootText:
Superadmin only
        Limits for every rota
        Limits are the boundaries every rota stays inside: how many duties one person can be given, how long they rest after a 24-hour duty, how many people each unit keeps free, and how evenly duties are shared within a call level. Generation, auto-fill and the extra-duty layer all follow them.
      
      History
    
    
      Hard limitHard rule: never broken. Generation, auto-fill and the extra-duty layer never go past it; only a superadmin allocation can, and that is recorded.
      Can be exceededCan be exceeded, with a reason, and is reported. Review and Publish warn you when it does.
      GuideGuide only: warns or steers, never stops a duty.
    
    
      Using the default limits; nothing has been saved on this page yet.
      View only. Only a superadmin can change limits.
    
    Per member each monthRest after a 24-hour dutyUnit staffingEqual duties within a call levelExtra duties (justice)
  
    
    
    
      Per member each monthHow many duties of each kind one member should get in a calendar month. Every unit and campus is counted together. Leave a box blank for no limit.
      
    
    
    
      
        Max 24-hour duties per member per month
        Can be exceeded
      
      The most 24-hour duties one member should get in a calendar month, counting all units and campuses together. Automatic filling will not give a member a duty that takes them past this number. A rota board member can still go past it on purpose by writing a reason, and the extra-duty step may go past it when the only other choice is leaving a duty empty. Anyone over the limit is listed on the Publish screen and in the audit report.
      Example Set to 6: a member who already has 6 twenty-four-hour duties in June is not offered a 7th by automatic filling. If the board gives them a 7th anyway, it needs a reason and the member shows as over the limit.
    
    
      
      
      duties
    
      Blank = no limit
    Saved: No limit
    
    
    
  
    
      
        Max weekend 24-hour duties per member per month
        Can be exceeded
      
      The most 24-hour duties on a Saturday or Sunday that one member should get in a month, all units together. These also count towards the 24-hour limit above. Automatic filling will not give a member a duty that takes them past this number. A rota board member can still go past it on purpose by writing a reason, and the extra-duty step may go past it when the only other choice is leaving a duty empty. Anyone over the limit is listed on the Publish screen and in the audit report.
      Example Set to 2: a member who has 24-hour duties on two Saturdays in June is not given a Sunday 24-hour duty that month by automatic filling.
    
    
      
      
      duties
    
      Blank = no limit
    Saved: No limit
    
    
    
  
    
      
        Max duties of one duty family per member per month
        Can be exceeded
      
      Every duty belongs to a family set in Rota Rules (for example Main, CB, RC or PAC). This is the most duties of one family a member should get in a month, so nobody does only one kind of work. Duties of every length count, not only 24-hour duties. Automatic filling will not give a member a duty that takes them past this number. A rota board member can still go past it on purpose by writing a reason, and the extra-duty step may go past it when the only other choice is leaving a duty empty. Anyone over the limit is listed on the Publish screen and in the audit report.
      Example Set to 4: a member who already has 4 Main duties in June (say two Main 3rd Call and two Main Co-3rd Call) can still get a CB or RC duty, but not a 5th Main duty.
    
    
      
      
      duties
    
      Blank = no limit
    Saved: No limit
    
    
    
  
    
      
        Max duties at one campus per member per month
        Can be exceeded
      
      The most duties one member should do at the same campus in a month. The campus is the campus of the unit the duty belongs to. Use it to share work between campuses. Automatic filling will not give a member a duty that takes them past this number. A rota board member can still go past it on purpose by writing a reason, and the extra-duty step may go past it when the only other choice is leaving a duty empty. Anyone over the limit is listed on the Publish screen and in the audit report.
      Example Set to 5: a member with 5 duties at one campus in June can still be placed at another campus, but not a 6th time at the same campus.
    
    
      
      
      duties
    
      Blank = no limit
    Saved: No limit
    
    
    
  
    
  
    
      Rest after a 24-hour dutyProtected time off after a 24-hour duty. The rest rule is never broken by any part of the rota.
      
    
    
    
      
        Rest after a 24-hour duty
        Hard limit
      
      The fewest hours a member must have off after a 24-hour duty ends before any other duty starts. This is a hard rule: automatic filling, the extra-duty step, manual assignment and superadmin allocation all refuse a duty that would cut the rest short. It also works the other way: a 24-hour duty cannot be given if it would end too close to a duty the member already has.
      Example Set to 24: after a 24-hour duty from Monday 8 am to Tuesday 8 am, the member's next duty can start on Wednesday at 8 am at the earliest.
    
    
      
      
      hours
    
      
    Saved: 24 hours
    
    
    
  
    
      
        No elective work the day after a 24-hour duty (policy record)
        Guide
      
      Records the department policy that a member gets no elective (daytime) work on the day after a 24-hour duty. The rota does not read this switch today: the day-after block is set for each duty in Rota Rules ("Blocks elective next day"), and every 24-hour duty already has it. Changing this switch does not change any rota.
      Example On: matches the Rota Rules setting, so a member who finishes a 24-hour duty on Tuesday morning is not given elective work on Tuesday.
    
    
      
        
        On
      
    Saved: On
    
    
    
  
    
  
    
      Unit staffingHow many members a unit must keep free for its normal work before its duties are flagged or held.
      
    
    
    
      
        Members a unit must keep free (default)
        Can be exceeded
      
      How many eligible members of a unit must still be free (not on leave, not resting after a 24-hour duty, not already on duty) after a duty is given out, so the unit can still do its normal work. Each unit usually has its own number in Unit management, also per call level; this default is used only where a unit or duty has no number of its own, and only while "Always keep the minimum free" is on. A duty that would leave fewer free is held: template generation avoids it and marks it for review, auto-fill leaves it open, a board member can still fill it with a reason, and the extra-duty step may fill it with a member from another unit.
      Example Set to 1: in a unit of 6 eligible members where 5 are on leave or resting, giving the last one a duty would leave nobody free, so the duty is held for the board to decide.
    
    
      
      
      members
    
      
    Saved: 1 member
    
    
    
  
    
      
        Warn when this share of a unit is unavailable
        Guide
      
      When this share (or more) of a unit's eligible members is unavailable on a day, because of leave, rest after a 24-hour duty or another duty, that day's duties in the unit are flagged "needs review". It is a warning, not a stop: template generation still fills the duty and marks it, auto-fill leaves it for a person to decide, and a board member who places someone gives a reason. It must be lower than the hard-block share below.
      Example Set to 30%: in a unit of 10 eligible members, a day with 3 of them unavailable gets a "needs review" flag.
    
    
      
      
      %
    
      
    Saved: 30%
    
    
    
  
    
      
        Hold duties when this share of a unit is unavailable
        Can be exceeded
      
      When this share (or more) of a unit's eligible members would be unavailable on a day, that day's duties in the unit are held (hard blocked) to protect the unit's normal work. Template generation avoids them and, if it has no other choice, marks them for review; auto-fill leaves them open; a board member can still fill one with a reason; and the extra-duty step may fill it with a member from another unit. It must be higher than the warning share above.
      Example With 30% warning and 40% hold, in a unit of 10 eligible members: 3 unavailable gives a warning, 4 unavailable holds the duty.
    
    
      
      
      %
    
      
    Saved: 40%
    
    
    
  
    
      
        Always keep the minimum free
        Can be exceeded
      
      When on, a unit never drops below its minimum number of free members (the unit's own number in Unit management, or the default above), even when the percentages would allow it. This matters most in small units, where one person is a large share. When off, only the two percentages are checked.
      Example On: a unit whose minimum is 2 keeps 2 members free whatever the percentages say. Off: the same unit can drop to 1 free as long as the share unavailable stays below the hold share.
    
    
      
        
        On
      
    Saved: On
    
    
    
  
    
  
    
      Equal duties within a call levelMembers of the same call level should end the month with almost the same number of duties, whatever campus they work at.
      
    
    
    
      
        Allowed difference in duties within a call level
        Guide
      
      Within each call level, every member's total duties for the month (all campuses together) should be almost the same. This is the largest difference allowed between the member with the most duties and the member with the fewest. The rota aims for it; when leave or rest make it impossible, the Publish screen shows a warning for that call level, but publishing is not stopped. Duties added by the extra-duty step or by a superadmin are shown separately when they cause the difference.
      Example Set to 1: 3rd call has 130 duties and 40 members, so the target is 3.25 (3 or 4 each). Totals of 3 and 4 are fine; a member with 2 while another has 4 (a difference of 2) is flagged.
    
    
      
      
      duties
    
      
    Saved: 1 duty
    
    
    
  
    
      
        How the target is worked out
        Guide
      
      Each call level's target is its duties in the month divided by its members available that month. "Automatic" is the only choice for now; the targets table shows the numbers for the chosen month.
      Example Automatic: 4th call with 62 duties and 20 members has a target of 3.1 duties each.
    
    
      
        Automatic (duties divided by members)
      
    Saved: Automatic (duties divided by members)
    
    
    
  
    
      
        Targets for November 2026
          Target = the call level's duty slots in the month ÷ its members available that month. With a gap of 1, the busiest and the least busy member of a level may differ by at most 1 duty.
        Month
      
      No targets for November 2026 yet. They appear once the month's duty slots exist (generate the template in Rota Template).
      The extra-duty layer and superadmin allocations may break equality; Publish and the 360° report show when they do.
    
  
    
      Extra duties (justice)When the extra-duty step must ask someone to do more, it first asks whoever has done the fewest extra duties recently.
      
    
    
    
      
        Months of extra-duty history to count
        Guide
      
      When the extra-duty step must give someone an extra duty, it first asks the members who have done the fewest extra duties recently. This sets how far back "recently" goes. A longer period remembers older extra duties; a shorter one lets them drop off sooner. It changes who is asked first, never whether a duty can be filled.
      Example Set to 12: when choosing for June 2026, an extra duty done in July 2025 still counts, but one done in May 2025 no longer does.
    
    
      
      
      months
    
      
    Saved: 12 months
    
    
    
  
    
  
    
      
      
      View onlyOnly a superadmin can change limits.

numeric.text: No elective work the day after a 24-hour duty (policy record)

font.family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif

numeric.text: Records the department policy that a member gets no elective (daytime) work on the day after a 24-hour duty. The rota does not read this switch today: the day-after block is set for each duty in Rota Rules ("Blocks elective next day"), and every 24-hour duty already has it. Changing this switch does not change any rota.

font.family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif

numeric.text: On: matches the Rota Rules setting, so a member who finishes a 24-hour duty on Tuesday morning is not given elective work on Tuesday.

font.family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif

numeric.text: How many eligible members of a unit must still be free (not on leave, not resting after a 24-hour duty, not already on duty) after a duty is given out, so the unit can still do its normal work. Each unit usually has its own number in Unit management, also per call level; this default is used only where a unit or duty has no number of its own, and only while "Always keep the minimum free" is on. A duty that would leave fewer free is held: template generation avoids it and marks it for review, auto-fill leaves it open, a board member can still fill it with a reason, and the extra-duty step may fill it with a member from another unit.

font.family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif

numeric.text: Set to 1: in a unit of 6 eligible members where 5 are on leave or resting, giving the last one a duty would leave nobody free, so the duty is held for the board to decide.

font.family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif

numeric.text: When this share (or more) of a unit's eligible members is unavailable on a day, because of leave, rest after a 24-hour duty or another duty, that day's duties in the unit are flagged "needs review". It is a warning, not a stop: template generation still fills the duty and marks it, auto-fill leaves it for a person to decide, and a board member who places someone gives a reason. It must be lower than the hard-block share below.

font.family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif

numeric.text: Set to 30%: in a unit of 10 eligible members, a day with 3 of them unavailable gets a "needs review" flag.

font.family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif

numeric.text: With 30% warning and 40% hold, in a unit of 10 eligible members: 3 unavailable gives a warning, 4 unavailable holds the duty.

font.family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif

numeric.text: On: a unit whose minimum is 2 keeps 2 members free whatever the percentages say. Off: the same unit can drop to 1 free as long as the share unavailable stays below the hold share.

font.family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif

numeric.text: Set to 1: 3rd call has 130 duties and 40 members, so the target is 3.25 (3 or 4 each). Totals of 3 and 4 are fine; a member with 2 while another has 4 (a difference of 2) is flagged.

font.family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif

numeric.text: Automatic: 4th call with 62 duties and 20 members has a target of 3.1 duties each.

font.family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif

numeric.text: Target = the call level's duty slots in the month ÷ its members available that month. With a gap of 1, the busiest and the least busy member of a level may differ by at most 1 duty.

font.family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif
Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif

numeric.text: No targets for November 2026 yet. They appear once the month's duty slots exist (generate the template in Rota Template).

font.family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif

numeric.text: The extra-duty layer and superadmin allocations may break equality; Publish and the 360° report show when they do.

font.family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", sans-serif

numeric.text: Set to 12: when choosing for June 2026, an extra duty done in July 2025 still counts, but one done in May 2025 no longer does.

baseline.rootText:
Compute Settings
      Use this computer for optional rota scoring. Other computers keep their own settings.
      Keep this page open while computing. Server computation is always the fallback.
      Generation on this browser uses: Server
      
      GPU setup checklist
      
      To use this computer's GPU:
      ✓ Browser GPU allowed by your deployment administrator (done)
      ✓ Browser supports WebGPU (done)
      ○ Tick Allow GPU computation on this browser below
      ○ Set Compute mode to Prefer local GPU (or Automatic after comparing)
      ○ Test Device passes (also checked automatically before each run)
      You can also choose Server or GPU in each generator window under Where to compute.
      
      
      Device preferences
       Allow GPU computation on this browser
      Compute mode
      Server
      Automatic — use measured results
      Prefer local GPU — pilot
      GPU power preference
        Browser default
        Prefer performance
        Prefer power saving
      
      Test this browser's GPU
      Test Device
      Reset device settings
      GPU selection and Automatic mode explained
      This is a browser hint. WebGPU cannot list every installed GPU or select NVIDIA by name.
      Chrome on Windows may ignore this preference and keep using its assigned GPU.
      NVIDIA or another GPU is missing
        Check graphics acceleration in browser settings, then open chrome://gpu (or edge://gpu) to inspect the browser-selected GPU.
        Set the browser's graphics preference to High performance in Windows Settings → System → Display → Graphics, restart the browser and retest.
        Chrome also documents chrome://flags/#force-high-performance-gpu as a browser-wide option requiring a restart.
        Do not bypass driver blocklists or enable unsafe WebGPU flags.
        These settings are controlled by you and the browser. This page cannot switch Windows GPU settings or combine multiple GPUs.
      
      Automatic uses the server unless an exact-result comparison on this device proves local execution
      is at least 20% faster, including network, transfer and validation time. Three runs per engine include cold GPU startup and full schedule validation. Results expire after seven days or when rota data changes.
      Small workloads stay on the server in Automatic mode. Prefer GPU can run supported numeric stages for testing; whole-month constraints and final validation stay on the server.
      
      No current device test. Test Device to check browser GPU availability.
      Download GPU diagnostics

      Compare engines on this month
      Comparison creates and cancels six proposals. It never applies assignments or publishes a rota.
      Enable GPU computation on this browser before comparing engines.
      
      Local computation is off until you enable it on this browser.

baseline.title: End-to-end rota website guide
baseline.rootText:
No-brainer operating guide
        How to run the Duty Rota website from start to finish
        Use this section when a new rota board member needs to understand the whole workflow, the terms on screen, and what to fix when something looks wrong.
      
      
        Start With Members
        Open Template
      
    

    
      Guide Map
      
        Phase 1: Data Readiness
        Phase 2: Rota Generation
        Duty Eligibility
        Monthly Workflow
        Website Sections
        Admin Tools
        Important Terms
        Scores And Blocks
        Problems And Fixes
        Final Checklist
      
    

    
      
        Phase 1
        Data Readiness And Setup
        Do this before rota generation. If this phase is weak, every later page will show wrong candidates, wrong warnings, or blocked publish.
      
      
        
          1. Members
          Confirm active people, call level, designation, duplicates, and aliases.
          Open Members
        
        
          2. Leave
          Enter or import leave for the target month and resolve unknown names.
          Open Leave
        
        
          3. Units
          Enter or import unit postings and fix unknown units or unmapped people.
          Open Units
        
        
          4. Rota Setup
          Select the month scope, included units, and setup rules before template generation.
          Open Setup
        
      
      Start with Department Members because every import depends on clean names.Load Leave only after member names and aliases are clean enough to match.Load Unit Management only after members are clean and the target month is selected.Use Rota Setup last, after people, leave, and unit postings are ready.Move to Rota Template only when Phase 1 has no unknown names, wrong months, or obvious setup gaps.
    

    
      
        Phase 2
        Rota Generation And Assignment
        Use this phase after Phase 1 is clean. The goal is to create the month template, assign people under each duty in call-wise order, and avoid unsafe shortcuts.
      
      
        
          1. Generate Template
          Open Rota Template, select the correct month, and generate the empty duty structure.
          Open Template
        
        
          2. Assign Duty-Wise
          Open each day and fill Main, CB, RC, PAC, and other duties separately.
          Assign Duties
        
        
          3. Check Candidates
          Use suggested candidates, leave warnings, unit fit, call level, and workload signals before saving.
          Open Review
        
        
          4. Use Auto-Fill Carefully
          Run Safe Auto-Fill only when source data is clean, then manually review every filled slot.
          Review Filled Slots
        
      
      Open Rota Template and confirm the month shown on screen is the month you want.Generate the empty template only after Phase 1 is complete.Switch to Statistics to confirm unit-wise, date-wise, weekend, duty-type, and call-level slot distribution.Read cluster labels beside units: Unit 1 (3A), Unit 1 (3B), or Unit 1 (3C) means that slot is restricted to that 3rd-call subgroup.Open one day at a time and review duties in fixed duty order.Under each duty, assign slots call-wise so the day is easy to read and audit.Prefer candidates without leave, unit mismatch, recent-duty, or workload warnings.If you override a warning, enter a reason that another board member can understand later.Use Safe Auto-Fill as a draft helper, not as final approval.After assignment, open Rota Review before publishing.
    

    
      Duty Eligibility: Category, Call Level, And Eligibility Groups
      Rota Rules has two different ideas that sound similar. Duty category describes the type of duty. Eligibility controls which people can actually do it.
      
        Duty categoryUsed for duty counting and grouping, such as Main duty, RC duty, Shift duty, PAC, or Schell duty. It is not a member list.
        Call levels allowedThe normal eligibility rule. Main 3rd Call should allow 3rd Call only. Main 1st Call should allow 1st Call only.
        Specific groups allowedUse this only when a smaller selected pool inside the allowed call level can do the duty, such as Schell eligible or PAC seniors.
        Groups excludedUse this when most of a call level can do a duty, but a named subgroup should not be used.
      
      For ordinary duties, set Call levels allowed and leave Specific groups allowed blank.For Main 3rd Call, choose 3rd Call in Call levels allowed. Do not create a separate Main duty member group.For Schell, PAC, Main Shift, RC Shift, or PB Shift, first create the eligibility group in Admin Tools > Eligibility Groups.Return to Rota Rules and select that group under Specific groups allowed for the relevant duty.Remember: Duty category affects rota counting and grouping; it does not decide the member list by itself.
    

    
      Monthly Workflow
      Sign in and open Overview to confirm the API is online.Open Department Members and confirm active people, historical people, position, and call level.Open Leave and enter or import all leave for the target month.Open Unit Management and enter or import each person's unit posting for the month.Open Rota Setup, select included units, confirm rules, and lock the month scope.Open Rota Template and generate the empty duty template.Open each day and assign people duty-wise in call order.Use Safe Auto-Fill only after people, leave, units, and setup are clean.Open Rota Review and clear open slots, hard blocks, warnings, workload issues, and exchanges.Open Publish & Export, complete final approval, publish the rota, and download Excel.
    

    
      
        Overview
        The starting dashboard. Use it to confirm workload trends, API health, and quick entry points before doing detailed rota work.
        If Overview cannot load, the backend or analysis API may be offline.Use it as a quick health check, not as the final rota approval page.
      
      
        Duty Analysis
        Shows historical duty burden, weekend load, duty categories, postings, promotions, and manual review items.
        Fix invalid names or unmapped duties before trusting historical fairness.Open a person profile when a number looks unusual.
      
      
        Department Members
        The master people list. A person must be correct here before they can be safely used in leave, unit posting, and rota assignment.
        Check active status, call level, designation, aliases, and duplicates.Historical members should not be used for new monthly duties unless intentionally reactivated.
      
      
        Leave
        Records who is unavailable and why. Leave affects candidate selection, warnings, hard blocks, and publish readiness.
        Import leave into the correct month.Resolve unknown names before generating or reviewing the rota.Check leave pressure when many people are unavailable on the same date.
      
      
        Unit Management
        Stores monthly unit postings. Unit availability controls which people are suitable for unit-specific duties.
        Import unit postings after member names are clean.Resolve unknown units and unknown people.Check unit staffing warnings before template generation.
      
      
        Rota Setup
        Defines the month scope, included units, and configuration used to create the duty template.
        Confirm month, included units, and rules before generating.Do not keep changing setup after assignments unless you understand the impact.
      
      
        Rota Template
        The main work area for daily duties. Open a day, review slots under each duty, check allocation statistics, and assign people in call-wise order.
        Look at Main, CB, RC, PAC, and other duty groups separately.Unit labels with (3A), (3B), or (3C) are restricted to that matching 3rd-call eligibility subgroup.Use Statistics to confirm the split by unit, day, Saturday, Sunday, duty type, call level, and forced review slots.Forced review means every unit was hard blocked, so the engine filled the least damaging unit instead of leaving the duty empty.Use candidates as guidance; lower priority score means the system prefers that person first.Override only with a clear reason.Fast mode is useful when a heavy month loads slowly.
      
      
        Rota Review
        The validation dashboard for open slots, warnings, hard blocks, workload balance, and exchange approvals.
        A hard block means fix the rota or enter a justified override.Open slots must be assigned before publish.If review loads too long, use the template and check backend status.
      
      
        Publish & Export
        The final approval page. It checks whether the rota is ready, records approval, and exports the Excel output.
        Do not publish with unresolved blockers.Warnings should be fixed or intentionally accepted.Download Excel only after the final published state is correct.
      
    

    
      Admin Tools
      
        Rota RulesControls each duty's allowed call levels, restricted eligibility groups, and duty category.
        Eligibility GroupsCreates selected member pools inside a parent call level for special duties such as Schell, PAC, Main Shift, RC Shift, or PB Shift.
        MappingsConnects messy imported duty names or member labels to clean system terms.
        Historical ImportLoads older rota data for analysis and fairness context.
        Login AccountsCreates and manages rota board, computer admin, and superadmin access.
        DiagnosticsShows backend counts, health signals, and raw diagnostic payloads for troubleshooting.
      
    

    
      Important Terms
      
        Duty slotOne duty requirement on one date that needs one assigned person.
        Duty categoryThe category of duty used for counting and grouping. It is not a group of people.
        Call levelThe duty seniority or call category used for matching people to slots.
        Eligibility groupA selected member pool inside one parent call level for special restricted duties.
        Unit postingWhere a person is posted for the selected month.
        CandidateA person suggested by the system as suitable for a slot, based on unit posting, call level, eligibility group, leave, rest, and workload.
        Priority scoreThe ranking number beside a suggested member. Lower is better. The system adds penalty points for same weekday/weekend duty load, total month duties, 24-hour duties, rest concerns, staffing pressure, and override needs.
        SafeA suggested member with no known person-specific leave, rest, call-level, subgroup, or validation blocker for that slot.
        Needs ReviewA suggested member may be usable, but the board must review a warning such as pending leave, staffing pressure, or another soft concern.
        BlockedA suggested member has a hard conflict such as approved leave, same-day duty, post-24hr rest block, or a validation error. Do not use unless the system allows an override and the board records a reason.
        Hard blockedA slot or review item has a serious rule conflict. It normally stops final publish until fixed. Examples include no eligible members, too few available members, hard safety thresholds, wrong call level, or wrong eligibility subgroup.
        Forced review slotA generated template slot where all units were hard blocked, but the engine still filled the fairest least-damaging unit so the rota sheet has no empty duty cell.
        WarningA softer problem that needs review but may be accepted with judgment.
        OverrideA deliberate decision to keep an assignment despite a rule concern. The reason should be clear enough for another board member to understand later.
        Safe Auto-FillAutomatic draft assignment that avoids known unsafe choices where possible.
      
    

    
      Suggested Members, Score, And Hard Blocks
      In the rota day popup, suggested members are only a decision aid. The board still has to decide and save the assignment.
      The system first finds people posted to the same unit on the slot date.It then applies the duty rule: allowed call level, eligibility group, and excluded group.It separates people into Safe, Needs Review, and Blocked.It calculates a priority score. Lower score means better suggested order.The strongest current fairness rule is same weekday/weekend load. For a Friday slot, people with fewer weekday duties rank higher. For a Saturday or Sunday slot, people with fewer weekend duties rank higher.After that, the score also considers total monthly duties, 24-hour duties, weekend 24-hour duties, same duty category, same campus, rest gap, staffing pressure, and override needs.Use Safe candidates first. Review candidates need board judgment and usually an override reason. Blocked candidates should normally be avoided.Hard blocked slots must be fixed before publish unless the workflow explicitly allows a justified override.
    

    
      
        Common Problems
        Page keeps loading: refresh once, check API status, then try a lighter view or fast mode.Person is missing: open Department Members and confirm active status and spelling.Wrong call level: update the member call level before assigning duties.No candidates: check leave, unit posting, call level, and rota setup scope.Publish disabled: open Rota Review and clear blockers first.
      
      
        Do Not Do
        Do not publish with unresolved hard blocks or unreviewed forced slots.Do not import files into the wrong month.Do not clear generated draft duties casually.Do not change rota rules mid-month without board agreement.Do not assume Safe Auto-Fill completed every slot correctly.
      
    

    
      Final Monthly Checklist
      Members checked.Leave imported and unresolved rows fixed.Unit postings imported and unresolved rows fixed.Rota setup confirmed.Template generated.Duty slots assigned call-wise under each duty.Rota Review warnings and blockers handled.Exchange requests approved or rejected.Publish checklist passed.Final Excel exported.
